[quote=the_crystalline_empire;61625924][b]July 21, 2028: The First Convention of Secession[/b]

It had been generally agreed by the Ducs of Rosenmarkke that the government was in the opening stages of its death throes, the July 5th declaration had kicked the dominoes and had opened the eyes of many to the reality.

Now as the four Duc of Rosenmarkke sat quietly in the home of the Duc of the northern Estate of Thýven, Erjk Drs, the Duc of Knygta and Deyn spoke.

It has been clear that the establishment is now no longer in full control, the legislature is gone, the emergency council is gone, and word tells me that among the officers there are talks of either a coup or some form of mass defection, 

Mass defection? Asked the duc of the central Estate Mittlemarkke.

Yes, replied the Duc of Knygta and Deyn.

They arrested the duc of Belgarde, stated Erjk Drs grimly.

Thats a violation of the Act of Settlement, intoned the Duc of Westmarkke.

What of this reunification movement? Do you think they have some legitimacy? The duc of Knygta and Deyn thinks so, stated Erjk Drs.

They are a bunch of men in wigs and canes, we dont even know if the masses really want unification or just a change in the government, replied the duc of Mittlemarkke.

Belgarde was already in contact with the king of Montfleur allegedly, replied the duc of Knygta and Deyn.

As was to be expected, scoffed the Duc of Mittlemarkke.

I am of the belief that secession has become inevitable, to secure at least the regions of Rosenmarkke, replied the duc of Westmarkke.

That is in direct contradiction of the doctrine of the Eternal Revolution, exclaimed the duc of Mittlemarkke, The doctrine clearly states unity of the revolutionary is a key mandate, 

The Eternal Revolution was just a fantasy by the regime, sighed the duc of Knygta and Deyn.

Yet we functioned! Shouted the duc of Mittlemarkke

Barely, replied Erjk Drs.

You are committing treason with these suggestions, declared the duc of Mittlemarkke.

No, we are saving the state, replied the duc of Westmarkke.

No, II will not take part in these discussions, intoned Mittlemarkke, You all should be shot, he declared moving out of the room.

And there goes the central portion of the country, intoned the duc of Knygta and Deyn.

Shall we meet again? Asked Erjk Drs.

Yes, the other two agreed.

[b]On the Silent Coup[/b]

From the start and foundation of the Rosenmarkket state in the year of 1815, where the noble triumvirate declared full independence from the Montfleurois state, the presence of democracy as a system of stability was highly doubted by these three men, indeed it wasnt until the 1840s that the olde establishment released their grip upon the electorate and permitted the first elections to occur, only to allow for another elite to rise in its place, having to be overthrown in the 1890s. 

It is thus in Rosenmarkket history we see a cycle of instability and of revolution prevail across the various triumvirates, initially starting as a popular revolution and slowly becoming a controlled elite revolution in the arms of the security state. 

By the emergence of the United States of Oceanice and the Lavian states cold war in the late 20th century, it became evident to the government of Rosenmarkke that popular revolutions were no longer an effective or safe tool of stability, it was hard to control the revolts, and there were concerns that foreign malactors would taint the process and introduce more unfavourable elements within the government and society.

It was in this that the state began its centralisation of the security forces and the shift towards the doctrine of the silent coup.

The doctrine of the silent coup was initially presented as a stopgap measure to ensure the continuity of the state, without having to rely on some uncontrollable populist movement, which could take the nation and the executive down an unfavourable international path. Former SCSID director James Ivern referred to it in his speech to the legislature following the 2005 coup as Indispensable and inseparable with the doctrines of the state.

It was under the post-2005 order that the SCSID moved the ideal of the coup from a stabilising and rare option of last resort into a method of coercion and state control, with the SCSID realising that if the executive had the threat of being removed, theyd be more compliant with the demands of the security state. 

Now naturally, the SCSID had portrayed itself as knowing what was right for the people, thereby justifying any nominally destabilising action as the planting of a seed of stability for the future. As a result of this the legislature learned to stop questioning the SCSID, fearing the immediate repercussions of what essentially would become a secret police.

As the 21st century has progressed, the SCSID grew in influence over the executive, with a law in 2014 permitting the head of the SCSID to sit on the executive council and act as a permanent adviser instead of a quiet watcher. Naturally, the constitutional ideal was that the Triumvirate was over the SCSID, but this dynamic shifted gradually as various opportunistic directors and triumvirs saw the increasing global society and feared the collapse of the Rosenmarkket order.

However, despite the growing power of the SCSID the element of formal state doctrine had not yet been implemented as a tool, mainly due to the moderate nature of the Rosenmarkket government in the early and mid 2010s, not yet radicalised by the rise in tensions between THEP and the EDU that appeared in the mid-2020s.

The first inklings of ideological leadership appeared in 2025 during the sal-baliz operation by THEP, where Rosenmarkke aided in the toppling of the islamist terrorist group on Shamat, of which the SCSID played a crucial intelligence role. However, the 2025 toppling shoved THEP into the international spotlight as an offensive organisation, thereby alerting the EDU to the potential of a competitor. It did not help that Vespurias and Rosenmarkke were considering a union of states at this point, threatening the Elseyran balance of power.

Now the SCSID, understanding the threat that the EDU posed to Rosenmarkke and to THEP was determined that they needed something more cohesive and populist than merely existing as a shadow organisation with legal coup abilities, as a result, in 2026 there moved within the SCSID ranks a plan to abolish the triumvirate completely and install a centralised regime to match those of the EDU states. 

This plan came to fruition in 2027 during the summer budget crisis where legislative infighting over the massive armed forces expenditures that had been racked up by the Sal-Baliz operation, and the demands of the triumvirate to streamline and modernise the armed forces due to setbacks experienced during the Sal-Baliz war. This infighting led to the creation of the Strømm plan in July of 2027, which moved to establish Polenne Strømm (a highly ideological Thrømm triumvir from Thýven) as the head of a newly created ideological movement known as Strømmism, which the SCSID envisioned as a mix of efficient technocracy. The plan moved forward in September of 2027 with the SCSID moving to put Strømm in power and suppressing popular dissent through conciliatory actions following her ascension.

However, to use the adage, the SCSID under-estimated exactly how ideological Strømm would become, with nationalistic theocracy entering the mix by January of 2028. This demand of the SCSID for efficient technocracy and budgetary reconciliation to move towards a strengthened state, and the wild and propagandistic movement of Strømmism would prove to be the weak point in the plan, leading to a period of over-centralisation, mass emergency creation, and hyper militarisation in the months leading up to the Rosenmarkket-Wuloosyan war.

Unfortunately, by March of 2028, the SCSID had realised that upon the outset of the Wuloosyan war, they had lost control. Indeed it was the death of Polenne in a bombing raid that sealed the fate of the collapse of the SCSID, and by April there remained little of the organisation to enforce the actions of the state, save for the brother whom teh council of 99 had installed as the successor to Strømm. 

By May of 2028, where the current situation in Rosenmarkke takes its roots, the loss of Rosenmarkke during the war proved to be the beginning of the long summer which has thusfar occurred.

Of course as we see the massive escalations and the attempts of the government to reassert dominance and a partial restoration of the old order, it begs the question of whether normalcy at this point is a possibility. Of which Id argue that too many crucial elements of the state have become too disjointed to permit a formal restoration, indeed the ascension of Iosef Begren, a hardline Strømmist, as the head of the SCSID following the failures of Randolf only show that the regime has begun to lean on its remaining ideological base, however, Begren, does not hold the same SCSID that existed prior to the war with Wuloosya, his network is scattered across various dissenting regions, and centralisation and coordination remains slow.

So at this point, whether this last ditch attempt at saving the state will succeed, remains in the hands of God himself. 

   - Henri dEstienne XVII (King of Montfleur)

[b]July 23, 2028: The Second Convention of Secession[/b]

I see the duc of Mittlemarkke has made himself unavailable once again, intoned Erjk Drs.

Unfortunately yes, I heard you ran a public poll on secession in Thýven, mentioned the duc of Knygta and Deyn.

Yes, two military officers have been watching me, the poll is online however, and we have restricted it to only citizens of Thýven, replied the duc of Thýven.

How is it faring? Asked the duc of Westmarkke.

Better than expected, reorganizing our territory to include the lands Rosenmarkke annexed back in January helps a lot, laughed Erjk Drs.

How about the Estate Legislature? Asked the duc of Westmarkke.

Some of our members have been arrested, and there are unionists who are operating sub-groups in the capital, replied the duc.

Secession is a risky business, right now Knygta and Deyn plans on seceding on August 1st, but we need to first gain assurances from the armed forces that are losing their loyalty that their operations later this week will work, replied the duc of Knygta and Deyn.

Mittlemarkke has no doubt informed the government, intoned Westmarkke.

Yes, which is why it is my hope the Strømmists are engaged in other matters, replied Knygta and Deyn.

Belgarde, smiled Westmarkke.

Exactly,

 Eyh, remind me, the islands sovietised their forces during the war no? Asked Thýven.

Yes, they did, replied Knygta and Deyn.

Did the government ever order them to reorganise? Thýven asked.

No, its actually why we have loyalists to Unionism in our region, or at least strong opposition to the Rosenmarkket government, the islands have always been their own thing, chuckled Knygta and Deyn.

As has Thýven, but, you are the largest economic sector, replied Thýven, Your leaving will cripple the regime politically at least, 

The markets have been closed since the massacre, the economy according to independent analysts is in recession right now, investors have fled since the war, replied Knygta and Deyn.

What a mess, sighed the duc of Thýven.

Well its about to get better, smiled Knygta and Deyn.

We hope, replied Westmarkke.

[b]July 24, 2025: Rumors of secession[/b]

It had started as an internet blog a week before, and quickly flooded the Rosenmarkket and Montfleurois internet to the point where local news stations were beginning to report on it, secession.

While the government of Rosenmarkke openly denied any such movement, and blamed it on Wuloosyan bad actors the evidence that could be sleuthed out in the regions was enough to make a conclusion that even if secession wasnt occurring something was.

As protests continued across the country, driven by the momentum of the massacre earlier in the month, there had begun to be signs of military non-compliance. For instance in one protest in the Thývenic city of Gossen, the guards that had been ordered into the city by the government were reported to be avoiding the protests that were forming, or in some cases actively joining them,

Then there were the indicators, independent polling taken between July 20-24 showed that out a poll of around 1,300 Rosenmarkket from across the country, support for the government was at 44% a radical and steep drop from the 75-80% that had occurred during the war against Wuloosya.

The government was loosing legitimacy, and to most, it had become clear that this was the case, the declaration had done things that no-one couldve predicted. 

The question now for most was When?, because in more autonomous regions it seemed that they were ready to leap from the nation into secession, however, the more cautious public voices warned of economic collapse and foreign attack.

So what was true? When was it to occur? And most importantly, how?
